stories.headline: Trump reverses course on Poland troops, sparking confusion and domestic political credit war
stories.summary: After the Pentagon halted a 4,000-soldier rotation to Poland, Trump announced 'an additional 5,000 troops' for Poland on Truth Social, citing his relationship with President Nawrocki. NATO allies expressed confusion about the net effect; Tusk publicly thanked Nawrocki, while PiS claimed the episode exposed the government's damaged ties with Washington.

stories.headline: False fire alarm at Nawrocki's family home triggers political storm over state security failures
stories.summary: Emergency services forced entry into an apartment belonging to a family member of President Nawrocki in Gdańsk after a fraudulent fire alarm SMS on Saturday evening. Prime Minister Tusk convened an emergency Sunday briefing with ministers and security services, called the incident sabotage, and accused PiS politicians who called it a government 'attack' of 'extreme cynicism or stupidity.' The episode generated intense partisan fighting over state competence and presidential security.

stories.headline: Krakow referendum recalls KO mayor Miszalski, opposition declares national harbinger
stories.summary: Krakow residents voted in a recall referendum on Sunday, with exit polls showing Mayor Aleksander Miszalski of Civic Coalition losing his position and the city council being dissolved. PiS, Confederation, and presidential palace figures celebrated the result as a warning to the Tusk government, with slogans 'Today Miszalski, next year Tusk.'

stories.headline: Orlen cuts fuel prices repeatedly while government advances windfall-profit tax
stories.summary: PKN Orlen cut wholesale fuel prices four times during the week and extended weekend retail discounts through end of August, while the government finalised a windfall-profit tax (windfall tax) bill that the minister of state assets said could cost Orlen approximately 6 billion PLN annually. Former CEO Obajtek publicly disputed Orlen's accusations against him.

stories.headline: Government-NBP standoff deepens as Tusk blocks board nominations and Glapiński loses court case
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tusk refused to countersign presidential nominations for NBP board vacancies, potentially leaving the central bank without the legal minimum of board members by November. Simultaneously, a court ruled Glapiński's reprimand of board member Paweł Mucha unlawful, and a Sejm commission accelerated proceedings toward a State Tribunal referral. Glapiński received the Lámfalussy Award in Budapest and NBP continued heavy gold purchases (reaching ~595 tonnes).

stories.headline: US reduces NATO commitments in Europe; 'NATO 3.0' doctrine discussed at Helsingborg foreign ministers meeting
stories.summary: NATO foreign ministers met in Helsingborg, Sweden ahead of the Ankara summit; a Reuters report said the US would inform allies of reductions to forces available under the NATO Force Model, while Gen. Grynkewich confirmed the withdrawal of an armored brigade from Poland. Commentary on a 'NATO 3.0' concept emerged, envisioning Europe taking full responsibility for conventional defence with the US providing nuclear cover.
